newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia merchant bank assets up in first half.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia merchant bank assets up in first half.

text.p: Malaysia's merchant bank assets rose by 8.9 percent to 29.5 billion ringgit in the first six months of 1996, versus a 6.9 percent rise in the first half of 1995, Bank Negara Malaysia said on Tuesday.

Deposits at merchant banks were up 22.2 percent to 19.7 billion ringgit at end June 1996, accounting for 6.3 percent of total deposits mobilised by the banking system, the central bank said in a statement.
Bank Negara is holding its annual weeklong meeting with Malaysian financial institutions.
It said the increase in deposits came mainly from financial institutions and business enterprises.
Loans rose by 16.1 percent in the first half of 1996 versus 4.4 percent in the corresponding 1995 period.

Non-performing loans fell 17.4 percent from 0.4 billion ringgit at the end of December 1995 to 0.3 billion ringgit at the end of June 1996. Coupled with an expansion in loans, the ratio of non-performing loans to total loans fell to 2.1 percent as at end-June 1996.
